note:
The findings that STAND. Each is a decision with the reason written down, not a defect left alone — there are three, and the suite fails the moment a fourth appears.

This list held 81 on 2026-08-21 before the fixing loop. The 78 that were fixed are not kept here as ghosts: what they were and what they meant is in DEFECTS.md sections 5 and 6, and in the commit history. Keeping fixed findings in this file would make every run print a long list of things that are no longer true, which is how a standing tool becomes one nobody reads.

known.fingerprint: schema/rawtext|the name check|a name containing a script tag was accepted unchanged; whether that is safe depends entire
known.what: a name containing a script tag was accepted unchanged; whether that is safe depends entirely on every screen that later prints it
known.why: Reviewed again 2026-08-21 during the fixing loop and DELIBERATELY LEFT AS IT IS. A name may contain any characters the owner wants to type, including "<" and a line break, and refusing them would take away a choice for no benefit. It is safe because both pages put a name through the escaping helper before drawing it, so markup in a name is shown as the text the owner typed rather than run as markup — and that escaping is itself checked by this suite on every run, including the case of an object reaching it. The finding stays on the list because the safety depends entirely on that escaping continuing to hold, and this line is what will notice if it stops.

known.fingerprint: ui/disagree|the "money" formatter, on both pages|the two pages format the same value differently in # of # cases: given a number written as
known.what: the two pages format the same value differently in 1 of 11 cases: given a number written as text, the Trade page shows "+12.5000" and the Construct page shows "$12.50". Two screens describing the same system that disagree leave no way to tell which one is right.
known.why: 2026-08-21, during the fixing loop. The BROKEN-value halves of this disagreement are fixed — neither page will now print NaN, Infinity, a boolean or an empty list where money belongs; both show a dash. What remains is purely presentational and DELIBERATE: the Trade page shows signed profit and loss to four places, which is what it has always shown and what the owner reads on the trading screen, and the Construct page shows dollars to two. Changing how the trading screen prints money is the owner decision this rule exists to protect, so the finding stays on the list rather than being quietly closed or the check quietly weakened.
